ELEBAKE(8) FreeBSD System Manager's Manual ELEBAKE(8)

NAME

elebake — compiler for a verified-boot trust chain (build, sign, deploy, attest)

SYNOPSIS

elebake command [args ...]

DESCRIPTION

elebake maintains the trust chain of a locally built FreeBSD boot loader: checked-out source, measured expectations, Authenticode signature, OpenPGP-attested manifest, deployment to removable boot media, and tamper witnesses read back at boot.

Every elebake command is a generator: it emits shell text describing an action. Whether that text is displayed, piped, or executed is decided by an interpreter the operator controls per function (see ENVIRONMENT). The shipped default displays (‘cat’): inspect first, then pin an executing interpreter. Batch commands emit an unconditional sequence of further elebake commands; checking is itself a command in the sequence, and the batch machinery stops at the first failure.

COMMANDS

The authoritative, always current command reference is built into the tool:

elebake help              # grouped command overview
elebake help <command>    # one command, parameters, examples
elebake help env [<VAR>]   # documented environment variables
elebake help intp <fn>     # interpreter resolution for a function

The command families, briefly:

bootstrap, init, environment
Create a database (bootstrap name profile), install a variable profile (environment init), manage the layered variable store (setenv, getenv, unsetenv, printenv) and the environment cache.
pem, openpgp, pkcs11
Key backends. Records hold paths and URIs only (material stays where it lives); add registers, dump emits the replay, import reproduces one extra record file, prerequisites checks the toolchain functionally.
stage
The staging object: a named workspace for one boot tree. add, checkout, build, install, include, sign, make form the build pipeline; sign-key, attest-key, filter, device, boot tree bind records; manifest, attest, verify, tree sync, deploy, push publish to a medium; marker, site mk, trust anchor, trust mk provision the measured expectations; dump, import, check stage migrate whole stages between databases; status, list derive state from the artifacts.
dump, restore, batch
Whole-database export as a replayable script (FILES), and its replay. The dump describes everything that is stored; the restore replays it idempotently (keep-going), build artifacts are regenerated, never moved.
help, help env, help intp, last, log, error
Documentation, trace inspection (last) and logging.

ENVIRONMENT

All configuration lives in ELEBAKE_* variables, layered as .env/local (override), .env/default (installed profile) and shipped templates. Key variables:

ELEBAKE_BASE
The active database (default ~/.elebake/db).
ELEBAKE_TERMINAL_INTERPRETER
What runs the emitted shell of terminals; default ‘cat’ (display). Pin ‘sh’ to execute.
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_<fn>
Per-function override, arity-specific (‘..._stage_import4’) before arity-agnostic. An agnostic pin covers the whole family and is only legal when the family is homogeneous.
ELEBAKE_FREEBSD_SRC, ELEBAKE_STAND_BUILD_SUBDIRS
Source repository and the curated stand/ component lists for the build.

Every variable is documented in place: ‘elebake help env <VAR>’.

FILES

~/.elebake/db
active database (symlink)
~/.elebake/current/.log/
per-invocation traces - the debugging ground truth
~/.elebake/worktree/
git worktrees of the FreeBSD source; build trees live outside the database

EXAMPLES

Create a database, register keys, build and publish a stage:

./elebake.sh bootstrap current minimal | sh
./elebake.sh pkcs11 add db 'pkcs11:token=...;object=db' /root/sb/db.crt
./elebake.sh openpgp add manifest 0123456789ABCDEF /root/sb/.gnupg
./elebake.sh stage add smoke1
./elebake.sh stage sign key smoke1 pkcs11 db
./elebake.sh stage attest key smoke1 openpgp manifest
./elebake.sh stage checkout smoke1 mybranch | sh
./elebake.sh stage make smoke1
./elebake.sh stage push smoke1 b

Migrate a database:

env ELEBAKE_BASE=$HOME/.old/current ./elebake.sh dump > mig.sh
./elebake.sh bootstrap current minimal | sh
./elebake.sh restore mig.sh

Inspect instead of act (any command): run it while the terminal default is ‘cat’, read the emitted shell, then re-run under an executing pin.
